ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, there are three intersecting circles, labeled ⊙A, ⊙B, and ⊙C. Points A, X, B, Y, C lie on the same horizontal line, and the order is A-X-B-Y-C. In the figure, point C is located at the horizontal right endpoint of circle B, so BC is the radius of circle B; point Y is located at the horizontal left endpoint of circle C, so CY is the radius of circle C, and Y is between B and C. Reasoning: The problem gives that the diameter of circle B is 20 inches, so the radius of circle B, BC=10 inches. The diameter of circle C is 14 inches, so the radius of circle C, CY=7 inches. Because B, Y, C are collinear and Y is between B and C, BY=BC-CY=10-7=3.

raw_record.question_text: The diameters of $\odot A$, $\odot B$, and $\odot C$ are 10 inches, 20 inches, and 14 inches, respectively. Find $BY$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: A, X, B, Y, and C lie on one horizontal line. Point C is shown on the circumference of circle B, so BC is a radius of circle B. Point Y is shown as the left intersection of circle C with the same horizontal line, so CY is a radius of circle C, with Y between B and C. From the text, the diameters of circles B and C are 20 and 14, so their radii are 10 and 7. Since the points are collinear in the order B-Y-C, compute BY = BC - CY = 10 - 7 = 3.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a one-dimensional coordinate setup along the horizontal centerline: place B at coordinate 0. The diagram shows C as the right-hand point where circle B meets the centerline, so C has coordinate +10 because circle B has radius 10 from its 20-inch diameter. The diagram also shows Y as the left-hand point of circle C on this line. Since circle C has radius 7 from its 14-inch diameter, Y is 7 units left of C, so its coordinate is 10 - 7 = 3. Therefore BY, the distance from coordinate 0 to coordinate 3, is 3.
